title: AOD Ring
tagline: An Android always-on display that draws a ring of light around the camera hole
summary: A native Android app that raises a black always-on screen over the keyguard and animates a ring of light around the front-camera punch-hole, with 12 light modes, per-app notification colours and battery-aware charging rings. The interesting parts are placement (Android only reports a padded keep-out rect, so a resolver plus a first-class drag-to-calibrate screen locate the lens) and a battery-conscious renderer: three translucent glow passes instead of blur, cached sweep gradients, 30 fps, burn-in drift. The portfolio demo is a Canvas 2D web simulator built on a line-for-line port of the Kotlin renderer.
highlights: 12 light modes (Breathe, Heartbeat, Comet, Aurora, Sparkle, Charge, Notify…) drawn with only Canvas/Paint/SweepGradient — no runtime dependencies
Glow is 4 layered strokes (widths 2.6/1.4/0.65/0 × glow, alphas 9/16/28/100%) instead of BlurMaskFilter, so it stays hardware-accelerated
CutoutResolver sizes the ring from the cutout rect's width and centres it on the rect, handling padded rects like the OnePlus 11R's 76×139 px keep-out, multiple rects and full-width notches
Burn-in mitigation: ±1.5 dp Lissajous drift over ~97 s, 30 fps frame cap, battery and proximity (pocket) gates
Notification-driven tint: each app's accent (or icon's dominant colour) is pushed to a legible HSV value and lent to whatever mode is running
polishNote: Thoughtful, well-documented native code and a gorgeous simulator, but the APK has never been run on a device per its own README.
